newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says arms cuts on hold until pact ratified.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says arms cuts on hold until pact ratified.

text.p: The United States said on Friday it would not proceed with deeper cuts in nuclear weapons until Russia's parliament overcome its opposition and ratified the START II treaty.
"One of the things the Russians are clearly interested in because they don't have a lot of money for their military is a START III treaty," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
"Of course we're not willing to go on to START III until we get START II," he added.

Defence Secretary William Perry -- on a visit to Moscow -- clashed with Russian legislators on Thursday in a hard-nosed exchange on nuclear arms cuts, apparently doing little to reverse overwhelming opposition to the START II treaty.

He pressed members of the State Duma, parliament's lower house, to ratify the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty (START), which would slash U.S. and Russian nuclear warheads to about 3,000 on each side by the year 2003 from more than 6,000 each.

But U.S. and Russian officials said afterward that START II, ratified by the U.S. Senate last January, remained in trouble because of deep Russian suspicions about NATO's planned expansion into eastern Europe.
Burns acknowledged that "clearly we're not on the verge of Russian Duma ratification. It's an uphill struggle at this point" to try to save the treaty.
But he insisted: "We're not planning on failure. We're planning on someday being successful. We're not giving up the fight."

He said that like the United States, Russia could not afford the status quo. Perry told Russian legislators that Russia and the United States could each save nearly $5 billion over five years by destroying warheads instead of maintaining huge arsenals.
